summary.headline: Pricol Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore at INR 1,077.9 crore, EBITDA margin 13.29%, but management guides to near-term earnings softening from geopolitical and input-cost headwinds.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was INR 1,077.9 crore with EBITDA of INR 143.28 crore (13.29% margin) and PAT of INR 73.23 crore (6.79% margin). For FY26, revenue was just under INR 4,000 crore (up 51.24%), EBITDA INR 492.91 crore (12.44% margin) and PAT INR 250.80 crore. Management said West Asia-related input cost spikes (polymers, aluminium, semiconductors, freight, rupee) will soften earnings, with cost recovery from OEMs still under negotiation. It is holding capex, R&D and dividend at prior levels, and plans INR 680-700 crore capex this year.

financial_highlights.change: 43.34% QoQ on comparable basis (as stated by management)
62.27% QoQ increase on comparable basis (as stated)
Excludes supplier and customer bill discounting, reclassified to borrowings under Ind AS regrouping

segments.name: DICVS
segments.commentary: Approximately 60% of FY26 consolidated revenue (management approximation). Digital instrument clusters; PV digital cluster share at TATA Motors about 75-80% of TATA cars.

segments.name: ACFMS
segments.commentary: Approximately 20% of FY26 revenue. Non-brake business about INR 750 crore in FY26 (96-97% of ACFMS revenue); management said FY26 growth was about 30%, but 30% growth outlook for the coming year is now uncertain.

segments.name: P3L (polymer/plastics)
segments.commentary: Approximately 20% of FY26 revenue; FY26 revenue INR 924 crore with EBITDA margin 9.24% per CFO. About INR 65 crore of contract foaming business transferred back to TVS in February 2026 will not continue. Management aims to double P3L turnover in three years from takeover.

guidance_outlook: Management expects softening of earnings and slowdown in the automotive sector due to geopolitical headwinds; it called the outlook bleak but said the company is confident of navigating it.

Recovery of input cost increases (polymers up about 55%, aluminium up about 62%, semiconductors up about 35%, memory control devices up about 28%, plus freight and rupee moves) is being pursued with top 10-12 customers via supplementary invoicing; management said full recovery from OEMs is unlikely and the picture should be clearer next quarter.
Management expects P3L margins to soften over two years due to forward investment (polymer technology centre, pre-hiring for new plants), with a return to about 10% normalised margin.
Management expects to keep growing above market growth rate, but could not give a firm FY27 growth number; ACFMS 30% growth outlook depends on conditions, with clarity expected around September.
Capex of INR 680-700 crore planned for the current year; debt-equity ratio expected around 0.5-0.6, below 1.
Dividend held at 200% (interim Golden Jubilee dividend already declared); Board to review after next six months.
Exports about 7% of revenue against a 20% target; goal is 10% in coming years.
Management aims to raise wallet share with about 10 strategic customers by at least 50% over three years.
capex_capacity: Next major capex cycle starts this year; planned capex of INR 680-700 crore across DICVS, ACFMS and polymer for new businesses, plants and machines.
Plastics unable to grow this year due to lack of capacity; capacity utilisation at peak, which management linked to high ROCE.
BOE Varitronix MoU: backlight module production expected in about 10-12 months (equipment and buildings in progress); management said it adds no incremental revenue, only backward integration.
Domino: ready in about 18-24 months, with early revenue to follow.
Honda account opened for clusters, pumps and plastics; TVS content already high.
Management is evaluating M&A in plastics and other areas with due diligence and active negotiations, but cautiously.
demand_pricing: Management said market share by volume was maintained and by value increased, per an external analyst study; confirmed LOIs cover most programmes, and no share loss is expected over three years barring market degrowth.
Competition is emerging: a group company of the largest OEM is entering instrument clusters and new competition is appearing at another OEM (per analyst channel checks).
Cost pass-through is a six-month lag; supplementary invoicing requested, and ACMA trade body engaged with OEMs. Management said a INR 25,000-30,000 price rise on a motorcycle could hurt demand.
Disc brakes: management reiterated its 2030 forecast; ABS is not in the product scope and development is not planned.

qa_highlights.question: How will market share in instrument clusters evolve over the next 2-3 years given new competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said share by volume was maintained and share by value increased; LOIs cover most programmes, so no share loss is expected barring market degrowth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY25 borrowing restated?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Ind AS circular required customer and vendor bill discounting, previously in trade payables, to be reclassified to borrowings; actual net debt is INR 63.11 crore at 31 March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13-15% growth guidance and P3L doubling target still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not predict the war's impact but expects growth above market rate; P3L is on track to double turnover in three years or exceed it, with new capacity being built.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook given cost pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost recovery is being negotiated through a tripartite process with OEMs and the company; management said full recovery is unlikely and next quarter should be clearer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the P3L revenue and margin for the quarter and year?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 P3L revenue was INR 924 crore with 9.24% EBITDA margin; Q4 margin was not given on the call, though an analyst cited about 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Will P3L margins revert to 10-10.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will forward invest in a polymer technology centre and pre-hire for new plants, so margins will soften over two years to about 10% before recovering.

qa_highlights.question: What is the content per vehicle outlook and capex for the next 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to lift wallet share with about 10 strategic customers by at least 50% in three years; capex this year is INR 680-700 crore, with debt-equity of about 0.5-0.6.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone other expenses rise 32% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to forex (rupee at about INR 95) and freight, which tracks revenue growth.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (polymers, aluminium, semiconductors, freight, rupee) and the extent of OEM price recovery, with the status expected next quarter.
Automotive demand softening if vehicle price increases hit two-wheeler demand.
ACFMS 30% growth target at risk; management will reassess after September.
P3L margin dip over two years from forward investment and hiring.
Competitive entry in instrument clusters from a group company of a large OEM.
Dividend reconsidered at H1 FY27 results after the 200% payout was held.
Exports at about 7% of revenue against a 20% target.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term plans and balance sheet, but cautious and at times evasive on near-term growth and margins, which management attributed to West Asia, rupee and crude moves. It gave no firm FY27 numbers and said earnings will soften in the short term.
key_quotes: So, while we are not scaling back on any of our critical activities that is going to hamper the growth of the company, we do believe that there will be softening of earnings and slowing of the whole automotive sector on account of these geopolitical headwinds
We have maintained our market share by volume and increased our market share by value.
So, we are starting a major cycle of CAPEX.
So, there will be some amount of debt, as I mentioned, but a very healthy amount of debt.

adds.what: BOE Varitronix backlight module production (MoU, backward integration, no incremental revenue)

growth.why: Management guides to above-market growth in FY27 but gives no firm number, flags softening earnings and at-risk 30% ACFMS growth, and backs it only partly with INR 680-700 crore capex, BOE Varitronix and Domino plants, and LOI-covered programmes.
